verdict.binding_limit: not memory -- (a) no import path existed for the published grid format, now written; (b) numerical robustness of a cell-centred FVM on a grid with 1256565 severely non-orthogonal faces
verdict.caveat: the configuration measured as stable uses first-order upwind convection, which is not a defensible workshop submission; no second-order configuration has been shown to survive this grid

grid.name: H6C1_RANS_3a
grid.family: R.1.TC1.01, HeldenMesh, Helden Series 03, fixed grid methodology
grid.acquisition: anonymous public HTTPS GET; no account, registration or participant identifier created or required
grid.header_length_crosscheck: predicted 89187516 from header counts, actual 89187516, exact
grid.units: inches; domain a 6000 inch cube, symmetry plane at y=0

import_path.problem: OpenFOAM v2606 ships no AFLR3 UGRID reader and no CGNS reader; verified against $FOAM_APPBIN. There was no path from the workshop grid store into this lab's solver.
import_path.solution: ugrid_to_foam.py, written from the format layout
import_path.validation: face orientation decided geometrically from owner-cell centroids, not from an assumed node-ordering convention; every computed boundary face asserted present in the file's own declared boundary list, with exact count match (145614 tri + 4175 quad = 149789)

convention_correction.documented_assumption: AFLR3 pyramid apex at local node 5, base (1,2,3,4)
convention_correction.first_attempt_result: 1505250 boundary triangles against 145614 declared; assertion refused the mesh
convention_correction.measured_truth: apex is local node 2 for 336700 of 341341 pyramids, median coplanarity margin 44x; base winds (0,3,4,1)

checkmesh.topology: all checks pass -- boundary definition, cell to face addressing, point usage, upper triangular ordering, face vertices, single region
checkmesh.comparison_a6: A6's mesh ran max non-orthogonality 70.4, average 18.9

memory.method: process-tree sampler at 0.2 s, reporting peak of summed RSS, sum of per-process VmHWM, and minimum host MemAvailable

scaling_law.basis: four-rung structured ladder at 334647 / 673920 / 1320300 / 2664180 cells, same solver stack, same 14 ranks -- a measured slope, not a single-point extrapolation
scaling_law.why_the_ladder_over-predicts: a structured hex mesh carries 3.0 internal faces per cell, the most of any element type; this grid carries 2.446, so the ladder is a conservative upper bound at equal cell count, and behaved like one
scaling_law.largest_grid_this_box_holds: roughly 15M cells structured, about 17M at this grid's face ratio, at 14 ranks, holding 6 GiB back

failures_observed.what: compressible path aborts in the thermophysical model
failures_observed.evidence: floating point exception raised in libfluidThermophysicalModels.so during iteration 3, after two clean SIMPLE iterations; logs/HLPW6_solve_np14.log

failures_observed.what: incompressible path diverges under default numerics
failures_observed.evidence: 14 iterations at falling residuals; iteration 15 GAMG pressure solve hit its 1000-iteration ceiling without converging (initial residual 0.017841335, final 0.009329799), continuity error to 3.6044204e+09, force coefficients to order 1e20; iteration 16 died with a floating point exception in Foam::divide(Field<double>&, const double&, const UList<double>&), a division by zero in the turbulence model; logs/HLPW6_solve_np14_incomp.log
failures_observed.cause: 1256565 severely non-orthogonal faces against a cell-centred finite volume discretisation

stable_configuration.settings: nNonOrthogonalCorrectors 2; bounded Gauss upwind for div(phi,U); GAMG with DICGaussSeidel smoothing capped at 100 iterations; relaxation p 0.2, U 0.3, k and omega 0.3; limitVelocity 300

force_coeffs_at_120.note: reference area left at 1 m2, so magnitudes are not yet meaningful; they are finite and evolving smoothly

stable_configuration.not_submittable_because: first-order upwind convection; a second-order entry is both dearer and less robust than what was measured

corrected_estimate.why_the_filed_rate_missed: not cell count -- rank count and grid type. A6 ran 4 ranks on a structured extruded mesh; this runs 14 ranks on an unstructured one, and parallel efficiency on this box is about 45%.
corrected_estimate.rank_sensitivity_note: 14 ranks buys 6.3x the wall speed for 2.23x the core-minutes; the core-minute price of this item is a property of how it is scheduled, not of the item
corrected_estimate.residual_uncertainty: the iteration count is still nobody's measurement. 3000 per angle is the docket's assumption carried forward unchanged. This is the defect that overran tmr-flatplate-finest-grids by 1.48x: the grid was priced and the iterations were not. At the upper angles steady RANS commonly refuses to settle and limit-cycles instead. The item is not bounded until one angle is run to its own convergence.

errors_found_in_the_filed_analysis.claim: the scaling is linear-in-cells from an incompressible run applied to a compressible one
errors_found_in_the_filed_analysis.correction: A6 ran DARhoSimpleCFoam, the compressible transonic solver, at M=0.850, per demo-output/website/dafoam/ladder-a/A6_crm_wingbody.md sections 1 and 2. The workshop case is the low-speed one at M=0.20. The stated mechanism for distrusting the number does not exist.

errors_found_in_the_filed_analysis.claim: ADJOINT_MEMORY_ENVELOPE.json (DAFoam succeeding at 63920 cells, failing at 99840) is independent evidence that the memory estimate is optimistic
errors_found_in_the_filed_analysis.correction: that envelope is entirely about the adjoint, and its own stated structural cause is OpenMDAO's reverse-mode sweep building a mesh-sized d[residuals]/d[vol_coords] Jacobian block. Test case 1 runs no adjoint. A primal RANS solve stores fields and one matrix, not a mesh-sized Jacobian. The envelope has no bearing on this item, and treating it as a bound is what made a routine 2.7M-cell primal look possibly infeasible.

the genuine risk was that no import path existed for the published grid format, and after that, numerical robustness on a grid built for node-centred codes. Neither appears anywhere in the filed basis.

consequences.for_this_item: feasible on this machine; no new hardware needed and none ever was; still underpriced, by 1.78x rather than by an unknown factor; residual uncertainty moved from memory to iteration count
consequences.for_the_five_behind_it: unblocked. They were sequenced behind an unresolved feasibility question on 36% of the backlog and that question is resolved.
consequences.reusable_asset: ugrid_to_foam.py. Every published HLPW, DPW and AEPW committee grid ships in this format or CGNS and this lab could read none of them before. Validated against a 2.66M-cell production grid to an exact boundary-face match.

still_open: compressible thermo abort untested against a temperature limiter
no second-order configuration shown to survive this grid's non-orthogonality
no angle run to convergence, so the iteration count remains an assumption
nothing here says the result would place well; this probe establishes that the case can run and what it costs, not that it is worth approving an approach to the organisers
compute_spent_basis: measured, not estimated: sum over every run recorded in measurements.jsonl of wall seconds times ranks over 60, counting parallel stages at 14 ranks and everything else at 1
